title: Context-aware sidecar doclets + tooltip flow for first-run scaffolding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a context-aware inline help system composed of compact doclets (anchor chips) that open a right-hand sidecar panel for richer content. The goal is to create a consistent, low-friction first-run experience that surfaces targeted docs links, short how-tos, and screenshots without disrupting task flow.
background: Stakeholders asked for an alternative to persistent tooltips and dense onboarding modals. Existing quickstart cards felt heavy and disconnected from the UI surface they explain. This work addresses: (1) discoverability of critical flows, (2) minimizing cognitive load during early product use, and (3) providing one-click access to docs/PRDs and short guided screenshots.
goals: Reduce time-to-first-success for common flows (model request, key setup, routing policy).
Provide contextual docs links surfaced in-place, with an optional expanded sidecar for detail.
Keep primary UI layout stable; avoid blocking modals or overlays that obscure inputs.
Meet WCAG AA contrast and keyboard accessibility for inline controls and sidecar.
Create reusable components for future onboarding flows and release feature tours.
proposed_designs: Hybrid pattern: compact doclet chip (icon + 1-line prompt) anchored to control -> opens sidecar with screenshots, short steps, and docs link.
Tooltip variant (lightweight) for extremely small contexts; auto-dismiss on blur or after 9s.
Collapsed micro-card in the rail for non-critical guidance (less intrusive).
Sidecar contents: header with micro-Breadcrumb, 2-3 step inline screenshots (annotated), quick copyable CLI/snippet, primary docs link, optional 'Try in sandbox' action.
Responsive behavior: on <= 900px width the sidecar becomes a bottom sheet; doclet chips remain inline but stack vertically.
A11y: doclet keyboard focus ring; sidecar tabbable and dismissible with Escape; ARIA live region for announcements.
tradeoffs: Sidecar increases DOM complexity and requires runtime mounting — tradeoff between initial bundle weight vs runtime insertion. Chosen: lazy-mount sidecar on first interaction to reduce initial JS.
Tooltip auto-dismiss reduces screen clutter but can hide important info. Mitigation: provide a persistent doclet chip that can re-open the sidecar and include a 'Don't show again' preference.
Tight anchoring to controls may cause overlap with dynamic elements (e.g., resizing panels). Mitigation: use collision detection + alternate anchor fallback.
Adding images/screenshots increases sidecar height; to avoid scroll jank we limit to 3 compressed screenshots and provide show/hide toggles.
review_notes: PM Liam O'Connor: prefers fewer micro-interactions; asked us to remove auto-open on hover for doclets — confirmed.
Engineering review (Kai Morales): flagged lazy-mount approach as acceptable but requested clear metrics for memory/perf impact — ENG follow-up ticket created.
Accessibility review (Ana Rodriguez): requested 4.5:1 contrast for doclet text; sidecar close target enlarged to 44px min touch area.
Design critique (2026-03-04): approved visual language; asked to try a muted accent color for doclet backgrounds to reduce perceived priority.
next_steps: Finalize Figma components: tokens for doclet, sidecar, screenshot annotations (owner: Maya, due: 2026-03-08).
Create engineering spec doc linking runtime behaviors and lazy-mount API (owner: Ravi, due: 2026-03-10).
Hand-off package: export components, copy strings, and acceptance criteria to Confluence and PR template.
Run accessibility checklist and keyboard-only flows in the staging build; log fixes as follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Doclet chip appears next to target control and is reachable by keyboard (Tab) and screen readers.
Clicking doclet opens sidecar in the right rail on desktop and bottom sheet on mobile.
Sidecar contains: title, 1-line summary, up to 3 annotated screenshots, primary docs link, and one action button (e.g., Try sandbox).
Performance: initial page bundle increase < 40KB gzipped due to lazy mount; sidecar mount latency < 120ms in staging on a 3G emulated device.
Accessibility: contrast and target sizes meet WCAG AA as verified by audit; all interactive elements have ARIA labels.
Analytics: impressions, opens, and CTA clicks emitted to telemetry for A/B evaluation.
